very_low_decisions_compact.reason: Large Dem. fish is a weak bottom-associated analogue. Taxonomy, reef or bathyal habitat, size and diadromous stages differ from source representatives; dedicated species groups are narrower. No split is required.
Large Pelagics is a weak open-water analogue. Body size, feeding, taxonomy or offshore habitat differs from the source mackerel and horse-mackerel representatives. No split is required.
Epifauna is a weak epibenthic analogue for echinoderms. Shellfish taxonomy, feeding and body form differ. No split is required.
Large Pelagics approximates the marine predatory phase of migratory salmonids. Freshwater stages, migration and taxonomy are not represented. No split is required.
Sharks & rays is a weak cartilaginous, benthic-feeding analogue for chimaeras. Holocephalan body form and bathyal habitat differ. No split is required.
Small pelagics is a weak forage-fish analogue based on source pearlside/Argentina. Taxonomy or bathypelagic depth differs. No split is required.

The provider-code bridge supports bony-fish scope, but residual composition across dedicated and pooled bony groups is unknown. Historical model-landings proportions proxy composition across the wider region, years and total catch including discards.
Sharks & rays preserves a taxonomic connection, but basking-shark filter feeding and size differ sharply from the predatory source sharks. No split is required.
The broad category mixes represented sharks/rays with chimaeras requiring a weak body-form and depth analogue. Composition is unknown; a single pooled group adds no split uncertainty.

Groundfish composition is unknown across dedicated and pooled bony groups, including benthic members of pelagic-named pools. Historical model-landings proportions add geographic, temporal and discard-transfer assumptions.

Pelagic bony-fish composition among Herring, Small pelagics and Large Pelagics is unknown; mixed pools also contain demersal members. Historical model-landings proportions add geographic, temporal and discard-transfer assumptions.

The broad demersal-invertebrate label has unknown composition across infauna, epifauna, crustaceans and benthic cephalopods in a mixed pool. Incomplete source catches trigger model-biomass weights with geographic, temporal and catch-basis transfer assumptions.

The broad marine-fish category has unknown composition across dedicated and pooled fish groups. Model-landings proportions proxy composition across the wider region, years and total catch including discards.

Historical order boundaries are heterogeneous and do not establish source-pool composition. Source landings proxy the split between Large Dem. fish and Small pelagics, transferred across region, years and catch bases.
Large Pelagics is a weak open-water analogue for tunas/billfish. Large body size, oceanic habitat and feeding differ from mackerel/horse-mackerel representatives. No split is required.
Historical order boundaries are heterogeneous and do not establish source-pool composition. Large Dem. fish is an assumed pooled placement; no split is required.
